subtitle: Helpful alt text comes from an image’s purpose, context and information, not its appearance alone. Learn to choose descriptions that tell readers what the image is there to convey.
scope: Learning is voluntary. Complete practice image accounts support private learning; this course does not certify actual output, authorize publication, invent service destinations or replace actual accessibility, assistance, editorial, records, privacy or equity responsibilities. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: What does someone need to understand or do with an image? Follow Elin and Ren through a diagram, a decorative border, a control and a figure. Corin and Anya bring different ideas about what makes a photograph meaningful. Practice describing the relevant information, asking about unfamiliar meanings and checking how the result helps the reader.

lessons.title: Begin with the image’s purpose
lessons.summary: Helpful alternative text represents the information or action an image contributes in its actual context. Start with that purpose rather than a fixed description of every visible detail.
lessons.objective: Identify the purpose of the practice two-arrow image.
objectives: Identify the purpose of the practice two-arrow image.
Choose a description preserving its actual instruction.
Distinguish an image’s meaning from unsupported conclusions about a page.
takeaways: Purpose depends on how the image is used.
A description should preserve the relevant information.
A useful sentence does not certify the whole page.
lessons.statement: Describe the information the reader needs from the image.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: What would be missing if the picture were unavailable?
intro.body:
Elin, a practice DHS staff member, prepares an optional practice page about reviewing a draft explanation. The page includes an original image of two arrows: one points from a box labeled Read the draft to a box labeled Mark an open question. Elin intends the image to explain the sequence in that exercise. Ren wants to understand what to do first and what follows. No actual page, service application or participant record is supplied in this example.

The first question is what the image contributes. It communicates a sequence, not merely the presence of arrows or a preference for a certain color. A description such as Two blue arrows could identify a visible feature while leaving the exercise unexplained. A description saying Read the draft, then mark an open question represents the supplied information more directly. It does not add a requirement to submit an application or claim that any real decision has been made.

W3C’s image tutorial and decision guidance distinguish informative, decorative and functional uses. The same picture can have a different purpose in a different context, so its file name or visual category does not settle what alternative text should communicate. In this practice, the boxes and arrows carry information needed for the task. If the full instruction were already supplied as nearby readable text, Elin would need to consider that context and avoid unnecessary repetition rather than mechanically paste the same description everywhere.

Alternative text is one way to provide a text account associated with an image. The actual method depends on the format and authoring arrangements. This course teaches how to choose the meaning to convey, not a universal menu sequence or a rule that every image needs the longest possible description. The proposed words should be examined in the actual page or document when real work is involved; writing a good sentence does not establish that the output presents it correctly.

An accurate account also retains the boundaries of the exercise. The image has no service deadline, contact number or eligibility result. Adding those details would not make it more helpful. It would create information absent from the source. DHS content guidance’s emphasis on purpose and clear instructions supports identifying what the reader needs without introducing an unsupported promise.

Privately state the purpose of the image and write a fitting text alternative. Explain one visible detail that matters to the task and one conclusion the description cannot establish. You can use the full example without creating a live page or asking another person to disclose a disability. The next lesson considers an image whose only supplied purpose is visual decoration, where adding words can obscure rather than improve the information.

inThisLesson: A proposed sentence and output review
lessons.keyStatement: Choose the text from the image’s purpose in context, not from appearance alone.

flashcards.back: The information or action the image contributes in its actual context.
A text account associated with an image that represents its relevant meaning or function.
An image carries information needed to understand the content.
The surrounding content and task that help determine what the image contributes.
A sentence to examine in the actual output, not evidence that it is already implemented.

accordion.heading: Connect the picture to the declared task

items.title: Identify the missing information
items.body: Without the image, Ren would need the move from reading the draft to marking an open question. The arrow’s exact shade is not the instructional relationship supplied here. Starting with that missing meaning helps Elin choose a useful account instead of listing visible features without explaining the task.

items.title: Read the surrounding content first
items.body: An image’s contribution depends on what the page already explains. If the same instruction is supplied as readable text, repeating it mechanically may add little. In this example the image carries the sequence, so the proposed alternative should retain it. Check the actual context rather than assume every reused image has the same purpose.

items.title: Keep the account within its source
items.body: The practice image does not include an application requirement or a service outcome. A more detailed sentence can still be less accurate if it adds those ideas. Elin can describe the actual instruction and retain the need to examine implementation without borrowing confidence from a professional-looking page.

tabs.heading: Compare three descriptions of the same image

tabs.label: Visible details alone
tabs.body: Two blue arrows names an appearance but leaves Ren to infer the required relationship between the boxes. It may be useful in another context focused on color or shape, but this page uses the arrows to explain sequence. Match the wording to that declared purpose rather than use a stock description.

tabs.label: The task meaning is preserved
tabs.body: Read the draft, then mark an open question identifies the supplied sequence. It does not invent a submission route or real decision. This is a fitting content proposal; the actual output still needs review to determine whether the text is associated with the image and available through relevant methods.

tabs.label: An extra obligation is added
tabs.body: Submit the required service application turns an optional draft exercise into a different task. Ren could receive a clearer-sounding but false instruction. Helpfulness depends on preserving the actual meaning, not making every description more forceful or adding a destination absent from the image.

check.question: Which description fits the image’s declared purpose?
check.correct: Read the draft, then mark an open question.
wrong: Two blue arrows, with no account of the task sequence.
The page is fully accessible because a description has been proposed.
check.feedbackCorrect: This represents the two-step practice sequence without adding an unsupported obligation.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Visible color alone omits the task relationship. An application instruction invents a different task. Proposed alternative text is not complete evidence about a page’s implementation or accessibility.

sorting.heading: Separate supplied purpose from fitting wording and unsupported additions

items.text: The image communicates a two-step exercise sequence.
Ren wants to know what comes before marking a question.
Describe reading the draft followed by marking an open question.
Examine the surrounding information before reusing a description.
The image includes a real application deadline.
A proposed sentence certifies the whole page.

lessons.next: Consider an image that contributes only decoration in its supplied context.

scenario.context: Elin proposes Two blue arrows for an image intended to explain reading the draft followed by marking an open question.
options: Whether a more impressive color name would sound professional.
Whether the wording preserves the actual sequence the image communicates.
Whether Ren will provide a medical history before she writes anything.
responses: A more precise color name still would not explain the task relationship.
This connects the description to the declared purpose.
Medical disclosure is not needed to identify the image’s supplied meaning.

lessons.transfer: Privately identify the image’s purpose and write one fitting description for the full example.

move.control: You can explain what information the description needs to preserve.
move.failure: Appearance, a false obligation or an untested assurance replaces the actual purpose.
move.next: Use the supplied image account; no live publication or another person’s disclosure is required.

lessons.title: Distinguish decoration from missing information
lessons.summary: An image used only for decoration should not receive words that invent information or repeat unrelated content. Determine its actual role before choosing the appropriate treatment in the output.
lessons.objective: Identify the supplied purpose of the ornamental border.
objectives: Identify the supplied purpose of the ornamental border.
Distinguish decorative treatment from hiding meaningful information.
Choose an accurate review question for the actual format.
takeaways: Decoration is a use in context, not a universal image category.
Meaningful information should not disappear under a decoration label.
A deliberate decorative treatment differs from an omitted or unresolved description.
lessons.statement: Keep needed information available without adding an invented explanation for decoration.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: What does the ornamental border contribute?
intro.body:
Elin’s practice page also has a narrow patterned border. The example explicitly says that its only purpose is visual decoration. It has no words, status marker, instruction, destination or information about the practice sequence. The page’s explanation does not depend on the pattern. This supplies a different context from the two-arrow image in the first lesson, which communicated the exercise’s sequence.

W3C’s decorative-image guidance explains that decorative images on a web page should receive an appropriate empty text alternative so they can be ignored by assistive technology. That is a deliberate treatment in the illustrated web context, not simply forgetting to consider the image. The course does not ask staff to write code or assume that a blank field in every authoring tool performs the same function. Actual formats and tools have their own ways to identify decoration, and the resulting output still needs examination.

Suppose Elin writes Required steps completed as the border’s description. She has introduced a status the image does not communicate. Suppose she instead labels every image decorative to avoid writing descriptions. That would remove the meaning of the two arrows as well as the border. Neither choice follows the actual supplied roles. Purposeful treatment should distinguish a visual ornament from meaningful task information.

This distinction is not a judgment that images lack value. A decorative pattern can contribute to the page’s appearance while carrying no additional information needed for the declared task. A photograph, symbol or similar pattern in another context could convey a specific concept or mark a meaningful transition. The author should examine the role in that context rather than decide that all borders, photographs or familiar icons must always be treated the same way.

Actual changes retain editorial and technical arrangements. Elin’s practice does not authorize someone to erase a real logo, remove required wording or hide an informative image from a published document. A proposed classification and treatment must fit the actual content and format. Missing or unexamined information should remain a review question rather than be covered with the word decorative.

Privately compare the border with the two-arrow image. Explain what would be lost if each were ignored, using only the supplied context. Name a question you would ask about actual output treatment without prescribing a universal software setting. You can complete this reflection from the example without working on a live page. The next lesson considers a functional image, where the explanation must identify what an action does instead of simply listing the image’s shape.

lessons.keyStatement: Decoration is determined by the image’s contribution in context, not by the desire to avoid review.

flashcards.back: The image adds no information needed to understand the supplied content or task.
The author identifies decoration appropriately for the actual format rather than ignoring the issue.
Meaningful content must remain available when another image is only decoration.
Whether the chosen treatment works as intended in the actual document or page.
An image whose role has not been established; not automatically decoration.

accordion.heading: Keep the two image roles distinct

items.title: Follow the border’s actual role
items.body: The example states that the pattern has no task information, words or status. Inventing a completion message would change the page’s meaning. Appropriate decorative treatment can retain the appearance without adding an unrelated explanation, while the actual format determines how that treatment is implemented and checked.

items.title: Preserve the arrows’ information
items.body: The arrows explain a sequence that the reader needs. Labeling them decorative would remove meaningful content in the first lesson’s context. The contrast shows why the author should examine each use rather than solve every image question with one classification or a policy of deleting descriptions.

items.title: Do not confuse unknown with decorative
items.body: If a real image’s purpose is unclear, investigate its relationship to the content instead of calling it decoration. A label cannot establish the role or repair missing information. Keep the review question open until the actual purpose and appropriate output treatment can be examined through the work’s real arrangements.

tabs.heading: Compare three treatments of the border

tabs.label: An invented status is described
tabs.body: Required steps completed sounds task-related but has no source in the ornament. The description would give Ren information the page never supplied. A text alternative should not serve as a place to insert a status, promise or new instruction simply because the image invites a field to be filled.

tabs.label: The actual decorative role is retained
tabs.body: The proposed treatment follows the supplied role and leaves the practice sequence available elsewhere through its own explanation. It does not require removing all imagery. The actual authoring format and output should still be examined so deliberate decoration is not confused with an unresolved missing alternative.

tabs.label: Everything is hidden as decoration
tabs.body: A blanket classification would cover both the ornamental border and the informative arrows. That discards the distinction the learner can identify. Use the actual contribution to decide, retaining meaningful information instead of prioritizing a shorter report or fewer authoring questions.

check.question: Which distinction matches the supplied context?
check.correct: The border adds decoration only, while the arrows communicate the practice sequence and need their information preserved.
wrong: Both images are decorative because that avoids writing any explanations.
The border proves all required steps are completed.
An unclear image should automatically be treated as decoration.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps the two roles distinct without inventing content or hiding the sequence.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A convenient classification cannot remove the arrows’ meaningful instruction. The border supplies no completion status. Unclear purpose needs investigation, not an automatic decoration label.

sorting.heading: Separate supplied roles from deliberate review and unsupported classification

items.text: The border has no task words or status in this example.
The arrows communicate the practice sequence.
Use treatment appropriate to the actual decorative web or document context.
Examine the output to distinguish deliberate decoration from an unresolved omission.
Every image can be hidden because explanations take effort.
Unclear purpose automatically means decoration.

lessons.next: Describe the function of an image that initiates an action.

scenario.context: The border is decoration only; the arrows carry a needed sequence. Elin proposes marking both decorative.
options: Hide every image so the review has fewer questions.
Retain the arrows’ information and consider appropriate decorative treatment only for the border’s supplied role.
responses: Neither image supplies a completed-work status.
Fewer questions do not justify removing needed information.
This follows the actual contributions instead of a blanket classification.

lessons.transfer: Privately compare what each supplied image contributes and what should remain available.

move.control: You can distinguish decoration from meaningful information without inventing status.
move.failure: A blanket label hides needed content or turns unknown purpose into decoration.
move.next: Use the full example; no code, live-page change or software demonstration is required.

lessons.title: Describe the action a functional image offers
lessons.summary: When an image is the only label for an action, its alternative should communicate that action or destination. A picture’s shape alone may leave the reader unable to identify what the control does.
lessons.objective: Identify the supplied action of the practice magnifying-glass control.
objectives: Identify the supplied action of the practice magnifying-glass control.
Choose wording that distinguishes the action from visual appearance.
Separate an accurate action label from actual function and navigation evidence.
takeaways: An action image has a functional purpose.
The description should fit the actual action or destination.
A fitting label does not prove that a control operates correctly.
lessons.statement: Identify what the action does rather than require the reader to guess from its shape.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: What happens when the reader selects the image?
intro.body:
The practice page includes a magnifying-glass image as the only visible label on a control. Its supplied action is Find a practice example. Elin intends it to help Ren locate an additional example within the practice learning exercise. The course supplies no actual search page or working control, and the action has nothing to do with submitting a service request or starting an application.

The image’s shape can suggest search to a person familiar with that convention, but the task is to identify the actual function. A description such as Silver magnifying glass represents an object rather than the offered action. Find a practice example follows the supplied purpose more closely. It does not promise that a real search succeeds or that any service request is submitted. W3C’s functional-image guidance distinguishes the action or destination from the visual object when the image itself supplies the control’s meaning.

Context matters again. If an actual control already has an adequate text label, the image might not need to repeat that same information. In this example the image is the only visible label, so the reader needs the action identified. The appropriate accessible name and implementation depend on the actual format and control. This is content reasoning, not instruction to paste one field into every tool or to assume that a label alone resolves keyboard interaction.

Elin should keep the offered action accurate. Ren needs to know whether selecting it finds a practice example, opens a page or submits information. Calling it Submit my application would invent a consequential action. Calling it Next without identifying the supplied purpose could conceal a distinction important to this page. The action should not require the reader to learn a private visual convention before understanding what is being offered.

The proposed words also need their limits stated honestly. In actual work, a fitting action label would still require relevant checks of implementation, navigation and behavior. Content staff can ask whether the text identifies the intended function; another actual examination must determine whether the control carries out that function. A practice label proposal does not authorize changing a live application or bypassing required review arrangements.

Privately choose wording for the supplied control and explain what it identifies. Then name one separate question about actual operation that the proposal cannot answer. You can reason from the example without clicking a live site or publishing an action. The next lesson turns to a personal encounter about what it means to describe a photograph, where familiar assumptions can add a story the chosen context has not supplied.

lessons.keyStatement: A functional image should communicate the offered action, while actual behavior remains a separate examination.

flashcards.back: An image used to initiate an action or lead to a destination.
Words identifying what selecting the control is intended to do.

An actual observation of whether the control carries out its intended function.
A consequential step absent from the supplied function.

accordion.heading: Connect the wording to the actual action

items.title: Distinguish an object from a function
items.body: Silver magnifying glass explains a visual object but not the particular action offered here. Find a practice example identifies the supplied purpose. The same object could serve another action in a different context, so its shape cannot establish what the user is about to initiate.

items.title: Retain the action’s scope
items.body: The example offers an educational example, not a service application. A description that advertises submission would change the reader’s understanding of the action. Clear wording should fit the actual function and destination rather than make an ordinary practice control sound more consequential or officially approved.

items.title: Keep content and operation distinct
items.body: A useful label can answer what the control is intended to do while leaving actual navigation and behavior open. The course supplies no implemented control. In real work, examine the relevant output and methods within actual arrangements rather than report successful operation from a sentence proposed in an exercise.

tabs.heading: Compare three labels for the control

tabs.label: The object is named
tabs.body: Silver magnifying glass may help someone picture the icon, but it leaves the offered task unexplained. The example supplies a specific action, so the alternative can communicate that function. Describing appearance is not always wrong; it is insufficient for this particular purpose and context.

tabs.label: The offered function is named
tabs.body: Find a practice example identifies what the supplied control offers. Ren receives a meaningful distinction without an invented service consequence. This supports content accuracy; the actual accessible name, navigation and result would still need examination if a real control were being prepared.

tabs.label: A different action is promised
tabs.body: Submit my application misrepresents an educational function as a consequential service step. Even if the icon were attractive or the sentence concise, the label would be inaccurate. Clear action language should preserve the actual function and keep unsupported destinations or obligations out of the account.

check.question: Which label fits the supplied functional image?
wrong: Silver magnifying glass, with no action identified.
All navigation is verified because the label is clear.
check.feedbackCorrect: This identifies the supplied educational function without claiming a tested result.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The object name omits the offered action. The application label invents a different function. Content clarity does not establish actual navigation or successful operation.

sorting.heading: Separate the offered action from relevant examination and unsupported behavior

items.text: The control is intended to find a practice example.
The function belongs to the practice learning exercise.
Check whether actual implementation exposes an accurate control name.
Examine relevant navigation and the real control’s result when actual work is involved.
Selecting it submits a real service application.
Proposed wording proves all keyboard interaction already works.

lessons.next: Examine how chosen personal context can change the meaning of a photograph.

scenario.prompt: Which revision follows the supplied function?
options: Find a practice example, while leaving actual operation to its relevant examination.
Submit my application, because action labels should sound important.
Remove all labels and assume every reader knows the icon.
responses: This communicates the offered action without inventing operation evidence.
Importance cannot justify a false action.
A familiar appearance does not replace the actual function’s meaning.

lessons.transfer: Privately propose an action label and a separate question about actual operation.

move.control: You can distinguish a function’s meaning from its visual object and untested behavior.
move.failure: An appearance description, false action or familiar convention substitutes for identifying the task.
move.next: Use the practice control; no real search, application submission or publication is required.

lessons.title: Let chosen context guide a photograph’s meaning
lessons.summary: A description should not add an assumed personal story to a photograph. Individually meanings the people describe can widen interpretation and change the response while leaving unknown identities and intentions unclaimed.
lessons.objective: Describe the two chosen learned meanings of a shared photograph.
objectives: Describe the two chosen learned meanings of a shared photograph.
Explain how a wider interpretation changes the description conversation.
Choose an accurate response without inferring identities or imposing disclosure.
takeaways: Visible appearance does not supply a person’s whole story.
Chosen personal context can change interpretation.
Understanding and technical image treatment are related but distinct questions.
lessons.statement: Represent the intended meaning without inventing the people’s identities, intentions or agreement.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: Remembering a shared achievement or recognizing shared preparation?
intro.body:
Consider a separate conversation. Corin and Anya are friends discussing a photograph for an optional neighborhood seed-sharing account. The photograph shows hands placing labels onto seed packets around a table. No other identity or emotional information is supplied. Corin initially proposes Celebrating our completed success. He explains that, in the neighborhood sports gatherings where he learned to keep group photographs, gathering around an object often marked a completed effort worth remembering. He brings that learned expectation to this image.

Anya chooses to explain a different meaning. In the family seed-saving exchanges where she learned to prepare labels, hands and packets together represented careful shared preparation before anyone knew which seeds would grow. Photographing that moment honored participation in the work, not a guaranteed result. For her, the proposed success description could erase the uncertainty that made the preparation meaningful. These are individually supplied practice contexts; they do not describe an entire age group, nationality or community.

The friends recognize that their initial readings concern different relationships between the image and time. Corin’s learned account connects a group photograph with completed achievement. Anya’s connects this kind of preparation image with care before an uncertain result. That contrast is more specific than a disagreement about whether to use cheerful words. Hearing the other meaning lets Corin reconsider why completed success is not supported by the supplied image or Anya’s intended account.

Their changed response is to ask what the photograph contributes to this particular seed-sharing account and keep its description within that purpose. If it represents the preparation, the description can identify hands preparing labeled seed packets around a table, with the accompanying account making the preparation’s meaning clear. They do not infer that the pictured people are relatives, name their identities or state that every seed grew. They also leave future participants’ reactions unconfirmed; no later answer is supplied.

The Council of Europe’s discussion of individual, varied cultural meanings supports understanding how chosen contexts can shape interpretation without turning them into fixed group rules. The personal insight includes noticing one’s own initial expectation, considering another account and responding differently. It can be valuable privately, even when you do not edit a workplace description. The story does not assess an orientation, require a biography or certify any image’s technical implementation.

Returning to Elin’s practice page, helpful image text should follow the actual meaning the image contributes. An accurate content choice still needs the appropriate output treatment and review. The two friends’ wider understanding cannot replace that technical examination. Privately compare their learned meanings and propose a response informed by both the image’s supplied information and the intended account. You may reflect without recording or sharing your own cultural history.

lessons.keyStatement: A chosen context can widen interpretation without authorizing an invented personal story.

flashcards.back: The personal setting and meaning an individual elects to explain.
A learned starting interpretation that can be reconsidered.
The particular information the photograph contributes to the surrounding content.
An identity, emotion, intention or outcome absent from the supplied information.
Personal insight is worthwhile on its own. You can keep your reflection private.

accordion.heading: Connect the meaning contrast to the response

items.title: Recognize Corin’s starting point
items.body: Corin learned to preserve group photographs as memories of completed shared effort. His proposed words follow that meaning but do not establish that this image records success. Recognizing the origin of the interpretation helps him reconsider it without treating his learning as a defect or requiring Anya to accept the conclusion.

items.title: Understand Anya’s preparation meaning
items.body: Anya’s seed-saving account honors care before an uncertain result. Completed success would change that relationship rather than simply make the description more positive. Her chosen explanation gives the friends a reason to clarify preparation and retain uncertainty without claiming that every family seed exchange has the same meaning.

items.title: Change the conversation and description
items.body: The friends ask what the photograph contributes here and choose words reflecting the supplied preparation rather than guaranteed growth. The response arises from the wider interpretation, not just a generic demand to be kind. Unknown identities and later reactions remain unknown, and private insight can stand without publishing a biography.

tabs.heading: Compare three responses to the photograph

tabs.label: Achievement is assumed
tabs.body: Corin’s initial success account becomes a conclusion about people and outcomes the image does not supply. After hearing Anya’s meaning, he can recognize why that description might misrepresent this preparation. A familiar photographic convention is context for his interpretation, not proof of the intended story.

tabs.label: Every personal detail is demanded
tabs.body: Requiring the pictured people’s histories before considering any description turns an ordinary content question into compelled disclosure. The example already supplies a chosen purpose and meaningful context. Unknown identities can remain unknown while the description communicates the relevant preparation without diagnosing anyone or making a group profile.

tabs.label: Purpose and uncertainty are retained
tabs.body: The proposed account identifies the preparation that matters to this use and keeps growth results unconfirmed. Corin’s understanding widens beyond the completed-achievement convention. The changed response preserves Anya’s meaning without claiming universal agreement, assessed development or technically verified image implementation.

check.question: Which response follows the supplied meaning contrast?
check.correct: Clarify the photograph’s purpose and describe the supplied preparation without inferring completed success or personal identities.
wrong: Assign the same preparation meaning to every member of Anya’s family.
State that all seeds grew because people gathered around the table.
Treat the friends’ understanding as complete technical certification of the image.
check.feedbackCorrect: This uses the chosen context to change the response while preserving what remains unknown.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An individual account does not define an entire family. Gathering around packets supplies no growth result. Wider personal understanding does not verify the output’s image treatment or every reading method.

sorting.heading: Separate chosen meaning from informed response and invented stories

items.text: Corin learned group photographs as remembrance of completed effort.
Anya learned preparation photographs as care before an uncertain result.
Ask what the image contributes to this seed-sharing account.
Retain preparation and leave growth results unconfirmed.
Every pictured person has the same identity and intention.
All seeds grew because the photograph shows packets and hands.

scenario.prompt: Which response reflects that wider understanding?
options: Keep Celebrating completed success as a universal truth.

Require a public biography and assessed orientation before writing anything.
responses: The interpretation remains unsupported by this image and intended account.
This changes the response in light of the chosen meaning while retaining the actual evidence.

lessons.transfer: Privately compare the two learned meanings and explain how the response changes without adding a story.

move.control: You can connect chosen meaning to a wider interpretation and more accurate response.
move.failure: A familiar convention, group profile or invented outcome replaces the actual context.
move.next: Private unrecorded reflection is valid; no personal history, assessment or workplace edit is required.

lessons.title: Keep a complex figure’s information complete
lessons.summary: A complex figure may need a brief identifying description and a fuller accessible account of its actual information. Preserve values, relationships and missing information rather than squeezing them into an unsupported conclusion.
lessons.objective: Identify the complete practice chart information.
objectives: Identify the complete practice chart information.
Choose a short description and a fuller account preserving its values and limits.
Distinguish a recorded zero from an unknown figure.
takeaways: A brief label cannot carry every complex relationship.
The fuller account should preserve the actual measure and values.
Unknown information is not zero or a reassuring result.
lessons.statement: Make the figure’s meaningful information available without inventing missing data.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: Three topics, two supplied counts and one unknown
intro.body:
The practice page ends with a figure about draft-topic notes. Its complete supplied information is Location has 2 notes, Wording has 0 notes and Sequence has no supplied count. The measure is Number of notes supplied for this draft-topic exercise. The figures are invented information about the exercise, not actual participant responses, service approvals or population findings. Ren wants to know which topic has a supplied count and which remains unknown.

If the graphic uses a bar for Location, a zero label for Wording and a question mark for Sequence, a description saying All topics have no concerns would misrepresent the data. The count concerns supplied notes, not an assessment of concerns. Wording’s recorded zero means zero supplied notes in this full example; it does not prove that every possible wording issue has been resolved. Sequence’s unknown count cannot become a zero-height bar merely to make the image look complete.

W3C’s complex-image guidance explains approaches using a short identifying description and a fuller account of the meaningful information. That fuller account can be part of the surrounding content, so it should be findable and understandable through the actual format. The course does not require every datum to be forced into one short field or prescribe a universal character limit. The purpose is to preserve the information and relationships the figure communicates.

For this practice, a short description can identify a figure of supplied draft-topic note counts and tell the reader where the fuller explanation is provided, if that location actually exists in the output. The fuller account should name the measure and each topic’s value or unknown status. Location’s 2 and Wording’s 0 have a known subtotal of 2 supplied notes for those two topics only. They cannot establish a complete three-topic total because Sequence remains unknown. A confident sum should not conceal a missing value.

No later figure or actual output review is supplied. Elin can propose appropriate information and a clear association without reporting that every reader already reaches it. In actual work, the particular format, text relationship, figure accuracy and reading task need examination within the owner’s arrangements. A good description does not grant permission to release real data or apply a practice missing-data practice as a complete agency rule.

Privately propose an identifying description and the fuller information account for the three topics. Explain why the unknown must remain visible and what the known subtotal does not establish. You can use the full example without creating a chart, collecting actual data or sharing private records. The final lesson brings purpose, descriptions and actual task feedback into an honest closing account.

lessons.keyStatement: A complete information account should preserve the measure, supplied values and unknown status.

flashcards.back: A visual carrying information or relationships beyond a brief identifying phrase.
A concise account naming the figure and, when accurate, the location of its fuller information.
An accessible explanation of the meaningful data and relationships the figure conveys.
Zero supplied notes for the stated topic and measure in this example.
No count is supplied; it is not zero or a conclusion about concerns.

accordion.heading: Preserve what each figure actually means

items.title: Name the measure before interpreting values
items.body: The chart counts supplied draft-topic notes, not unresolved concerns or approved services. Ren needs that measure to understand what 2 and 0 refer to. A description claiming no concerns would replace the actual measure with an unsupported evaluation, even though the visual could still show recognizable bars.

items.title: Keep Sequence’s information gap visible
items.body: Sequence has no supplied count, so its status cannot be completed with zero for visual convenience. A fuller explanation can state that gap directly. This preserves the difference between Wording’s recorded zero and Sequence’s unknown rather than require the reader to infer it from a question mark or empty space.

items.title: Connect short and fuller accounts
items.body: The brief description identifies the figure, while the fuller explanation carries the actual values and relationships. A location reference must match the real output. In this example you can propose that connection, but cannot claim that it is implemented or that all readers find it successfully without actual examination.

tabs.heading: Compare three accounts of the same figure

tabs.label: A reassuring conclusion replaces the measure
tabs.body: All topics have no concerns treats supplied-note counts as a complete evaluation. It also fills Sequence’s missing figure with reassurance. The description is shorter but less accurate. Preserve the stated measure and information states instead of assigning an outcome the chart never reports.

tabs.label: The counts and unknown are represented
tabs.body: The fuller account identifies Location’s 2 supplied notes, Wording’s 0 and Sequence’s unknown, with a clear measure. A short description helps identify that account. The known subtotal concerns only the two supplied topics; actual association and reading tasks still need review when an output is prepared.

tabs.label: A three-topic total is assumed
tabs.body: Adding 2 and 0 produces a subtotal for the known figures, not a total including an unknown. Calling the total 2 would make missing information disappear. The mathematical operation can be correct while the scope of its label is wrong; the description should retain that distinction.

check.question: Which account preserves the complete supplied information?
check.correct: Location has 2 supplied notes, Wording has 0 and Sequence is unknown; the known subtotal of 2 is not a complete three-topic total.
wrong: All topics have no concerns because the chart is short.
Sequence has 0 notes because no figure was supplied.
The complete three-topic total is 2 despite Sequence’s unknown count.
check.feedbackCorrect: This retains the measure, recorded zero, unknown and subtotal’s actual scope.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Note counts do not establish an absence of concerns. Missing information cannot be converted to zero. Adding the known figures does not supply the missing topic or establish the complete total.

sorting.heading: Separate supplied values from an accurate proposal and unsupported inference

items.text: Location has 2 supplied notes in the exercise.
Wording has 0 supplied notes and Sequence has no supplied count.
Provide a fuller account naming the measure and each information state.
Identify the figure and its actual fuller-description location.
Sequence’s missing count proves it has no concerns.
The known subtotal establishes the complete three-topic total.

lessons.next: Close with specific task feedback and keep unresolved outcomes visible.

scenario.context: Elin has Location 2, Wording 0 and Sequence unknown. She wants the chart description to explain its complete information.
options: Turn Sequence into zero so every topic has a bar.
Call the complete total 2 and omit the unknown.
Name the measure and all three information states in a findable fuller account, with an accurate identifying description.
responses: Visual completeness does not justify inventing a count.
The known subtotal cannot include an unknown figure.
This preserves the supplied information and identifies what an actual output must make available.

lessons.transfer: Privately propose the short and fuller accounts and explain the known subtotal’s scope.

move.control: You can preserve complex information without filling its gaps or changing its measure.
move.failure: A brief reassurance, invented zero or mislabeled total replaces the actual figures.
move.next: Use the complete practice counts; no actual data collection, chart publication or private record is needed.

lessons.title: Review the explanation in its actual context
lessons.summary: Helpful proposed wording needs examination in the real output when actual work is involved. Specific task feedback can guide follow-through without proving every method or outcome.
lessons.objective: Describe the three supplied practice responses accurately.
objectives: Describe the three supplied practice responses accurately.
Distinguish content feedback from untested output and broader outcome claims.
Choose next work that preserves actual responsibilities and private learning.
takeaways: A useful response concerns the task it actually describes.
Optional reflection does not replace required work or certify an output.
lessons.statement: Recognize useful progress while retaining the questions the evidence does not answer.

image.caption: Five people sit around a white table with laptops, notebooks and a drink beside a wall display and posted notes.

intro.heading: What changed in the reader’s task?
intro.body:
The practice closes with three chosen practice responses to the proposed descriptions. Reader A says the two-step wording made the exercise’s sequence clear. Reader B says Find a practice example identified the offered action. No answer is supplied from Reader C about locating the fuller chart account. These are the complete invented responses. The course does not supply an implemented page, actual keyboard test, demographic comparison or later service result.

Elin can describe A’s response as evidence about the sequence explanation and B’s about the action’s meaning within this example. Neither response establishes that the proposed words have been implemented correctly in every format or that the actual control operates as intended. C’s missing answer establishes neither a success nor a problem, and it does not prove unwillingness to participate. A meaningful closing account can retain the positive responses and the unanswered task without converting either into something broader.

The next-work proposal should follow the remaining question. An actual output would need examination of whether the fuller chart explanation is available, associated appropriately and findable through the relevant methods. Content review also retains the stated measure, values and unknown count. If the image’s purpose or surrounding text changes in a later version, the description should be reconsidered in that new context rather than treated as permanently correct because its earlier words were useful.

Minnesota’s adopted accessibility standard retains its actual applicability, requirements and owner arrangements. Selected image practices do not constitute the whole standard or authorize a person to decide an exception. Real assistance needs retain their actual appropriate timely arrangements; completing this optional course cannot be a gate to help. Actual editorial authority, security, privacy and records responsibilities also remain when real images or data are involved.

DHS Equity Policy’s actual daily work and qualifying formal procedures remain distinct from the reflection. Where the formal procedure applies, the required toolkit analysis or scan, or relevant customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director, is not fulfilled simply by writing one image description. Within One DSD, the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback. Staff remain responsible for their own work and can seek support without an invented mandatory consultant gate for every description.

Personal understanding also belongs in the learning. Corin and Anya’s encounter shows why a familiar photograph might invite a learned interpretation that another chosen account can widen. You can recognize a similar possibility privately without sharing a biography or editing a real page. Learning is voluntary. Privately write a closing account of the three supplied responses and one relevant next examination, or reflect on the meaning contrast without recording it.

lessons.keyStatement: Keep the observed task, the missing answer and actual responsibilities distinct.

flashcards.back: A specific chosen statement about the supplied practice question.
No actual implementation evidence has been supplied for the proposed wording.
An answer not present in the complete account, without an inferred motive or result.
A new use or surrounding explanation that may require reconsidering an earlier description.
Personal understanding that can remain unrecorded and does not need a live-work product.

accordion.heading: Make the closing account specific enough to use

items.title: Retain the useful task observations
items.body: A describes the two-step meaning and B the action label. Naming their actual topics keeps the feedback useful without enlarging it into universal operation or conformance. A sentence can improve an explanation while a separate output question remains open. The account should preserve that distinction rather than reduce everything to good or bad.

items.title: Identify the unanswered task
items.body: C’s answer about the fuller chart account is not supplied. Elin can name that question and the relevant actual examination without guessing a motive, treating quiet as approval or assigning a zero to missing data. The next work should investigate the task through appropriate methods, not demand a biography from the reader.

items.title: Keep learning separate from actual authorization
items.body: A private exercise can build judgment without approving publication, certifying an output or replacing a required policy procedure. Staff own actual work and can seek consultant guidance within the program. The full example offers a valid learning path without a real-file edit, colleague’s disclosure or public completion proof.

tabs.label: Universal access is declared
tabs.body: Two specific responses become proof that every image, format and control works for everyone. The claim leaves C’s task and all untested implementation questions out. Useful content feedback can be recognized without that expansion; describe what each reader actually said and what the example never tested.

tabs.label: Missing feedback becomes personal judgment
tabs.body: Elin records that C declined because the chart did not matter. The supplied account contains no such explanation. The missing answer should remain a question about finding the fuller description rather than a story about a person’s interest, identity or ability. Actual follow-up should respect that distinction.

tabs.label: Progress and open work remain visible
tabs.body: The closing account retains A’s sequence response, B’s action response and C’s unknown task. It proposes relevant examination while retaining real requirements and authorized arrangements. This connects learning to practical next work without pretending that selected feedback is a full certification or agency outcome.

check.question: Which closing account follows the full example?
check.correct: A understood the sequence, B identified the action and C’s fuller-description location answer remains unknown; actual output review and duties stay separate.
wrong: Two responses certify every image and control in every format.
C’s missing answer proves the chart account was easy to find.
One description exercise fulfills all qualifying formal equity analysis requirements.
check.feedbackCorrect: This preserves the two specific responses, missing answer and actual boundaries of the work.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Limited content feedback does not certify every implementation or method. Missing feedback establishes no successful task result. Optional description practice does not by itself complete the policy’s qualifying formal analysis procedure.

sorting.heading: Separate the supplied task feedback from next work and unsupported outcomes

items.text: A says the two-step wording made the sequence clear.
B says the action label identified the offered function.
Examine how an actual output makes the fuller chart account findable.
Reconsider a description when its actual purpose or surrounding content changes.
C’s missing answer proves success.
Two practice responses establish every service and population result.

lessons.next: Use the job aid for private learning or an appropriately authorized image review.

scenario.context: A and B supplied specific useful responses. C’s answer about the fuller chart explanation is missing.
options: Describe the two responses, retain the unknown and identify relevant actual examination without a universal outcome claim.
Certify every page because two readers responded positively.
Record that C was uninterested even though no reason is supplied.
responses: This recognizes progress and keeps follow-through honest.
Two limited statements cannot certify the whole output.
An absent answer is not evidence of a person’s motive.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain the three response states and relevant next work, or reflect on Corin and Anya’s chosen meanings.

move.control: You can recognize progress without inventing missing answers or substituting optional learning for actual duties.
move.failure: Task feedback becomes universal proof, or missing information becomes reassurance or personal judgment.
move.next: Use the full example or private unrecorded insight; no live publication, biography or public completion proof is required.

jobAid.title: Write image text from purpose and context
jobAid.subtitle: Preserve information and function, distinguish decoration and keep complex figures complete.

sections.heading: Identify what the image contributes
items: Ask what the reader needs from the image in its actual context. The original arrows communicate reading the draft followed by marking an open question; their shade alone is not that relationship.
Use surrounding content to identify what is already explained. A fixed stock description or a file name cannot determine the image’s purpose in every use.

sections.heading: Keep decoration distinct
items: The practice border is visual decoration only. Appropriate deliberate treatment differs from an omitted or unexamined description; use the actual format and examine the output.
Do not hide an informative image because labeling everything decorative seems convenient. Unknown purpose needs investigation, not an automatic classification or an invented completion status.

sections.heading: Communicate the actual action
items: When an image alone identifies a control, describe the offered action or destination. The supplied function is Find a practice example, not a service application.
Meaningful wording and actual implementation are different questions. Examine the real accessible name, relevant navigation and operation within actual arrangements when real work is involved.

sections.heading: Keep personal context accurate
items: Corin’s learned achievement meaning and Anya’s learned preparation meaning widen the interpretation of the seed-sharing photograph. Their response changes to asking its purpose and retaining uncertainty rather than claiming successful growth.

Chosen accounts are individual and contextual. Do not invent pictured identities, emotions or outcomes, require biographies or assign personal assessment positions. Private understanding is meaningful without a live edit.

sections.heading: Represent complex information
items: A short description can identify the figure and an actual location for its fuller explanation. The fuller account should preserve meaningful values, relationships and the stated measure.

In the full example, Location has 2 supplied notes, Wording has 0 and Sequence is unknown. The known subtotal of 2 covers only the supplied topics; it is not a complete three-topic total or an absence-of-concerns result.

sections.heading: Describe evidence and next work honestly
items: A’s sequence response and B’s action response are specific feedback. C’s missing fuller-description-location answer remains unknown; it supplies no successful task, failure, motive or population conclusion.

Reconsider descriptions when the actual purpose or surrounding content changes. A proposed sentence and selected feedback do not certify output, authorize release or replace actual assistance, accessibility, records and editorial arrangements.

Qualifying formal DHS equity analysis procedures retain their actual requirements. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback; staff own their work and can use support without a new mandatory review gate for every description. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.

remember: Helpful wording follows actual purpose and evidence. A concise sentence is not improved by adding an unsupported action, personal story or outcome.
Use the full example or private unrecorded reflection. No real image upload, biography, public proof or live-work edit is required.

sources.title: W3C: Images tutorial
sources.note: Actual purpose/context distinctions support image text that represents information or function, rather than one description reused without examining context.

sources.title: W3C: Alternative-text decision tree
sources.note: Actual web-context questions distinguish information, actions, redundancy and decoration; the decision tree expressly does not cover every case.

sources.title: W3C: Informative images
sources.note: Actual meaning and context support the original diagram account; the course does not invent identities, emotional states or unsupported personal stories.

sources.title: W3C: Decorative images
sources.note: Deliberate treatment of decoration in the illustrated web context is distinguished from an unresolved omission or hiding needed information.

sources.title: W3C: Functional images
sources.note: Actual action or destination, rather than only object appearance, guides the original practice-control label; no implemented function is claimed.

sources.title: W3C: Complex images
sources.note: A short identification and fuller accessible explanation can make values and missing information understandable in the example. Their connection to the delivered output still needs examination.

sources.title: Minnesota State Digital Accessibility Standard
sources.note: Actual adopted requirements, applicability, owner responsibilities and exceptions remain distinct from selected optional image practices.

sources.title: DHS: Content and writing guidelines
sources.note: Actual purpose, audience, accuracy, instructions and action labels inform the original examples without authorizing a service promise.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Individual and context-dependent learned meanings, self/other understanding and response support the original Corin/Anya encounter without group predictions or personal assessment.
